extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, hospital finance and payroll staff, Medicare payment stakeholders, hospital counsel, MGCRB applicants, and CMS regional/contract staff
extracted.subtask_short: IPPS wage index calculation and reclassification
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for computing the IPPS hospital wage index (including steps for salaries/hours, overhead allocation, ECI adjustments, rounding, occupational mix adjustment) and for hospital geographic reclassification (§412.103 and MGCRB) for Medicare payment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Hours calculation (Step 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute total hours using the same methods as described for salaries in Step 2. The formula for Total Hours (from Worksheet S-3, Part II) is: ((Line 1 + Line 28 + Line 33 + Line 35) − (Line 2 + Line 3 + Line 4.01 + Line 5 + Line 6 + Line 7 + Line 7.01 + Line 8 + Line 9 + Line 10)) + (Line 11 + Line 12 + Line 13 + Line 14.01 + 14.02 + Line 15 + Line 15.01 + Line 15.02). For FY 2027 CMS proposes to include Lines 15, 15.01 and 15.02 in this calculation and to use Lines 15.01 and 15.02 instead of Line 15 for future fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all hours except wage-related costs (which have no associated hours). Follow Worksheet S-3, Part II line-item conventions; note FY2027 inclusion/change of Lines 15 series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded area hours ratio and allocation of overhead (Step 4 - excluded rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the “excluded rate” as the ratio of excluded area hours to Revised Total Hours (from Worksheet S-3, Part II) using: (Line 9 + Line 10)/(Line 1 + Line 28 + Line 33 + Line 35)−(Lines 2, 3, 4.01, 5, 6, 7, 7.01, and 8 and Lines 26 through 43).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiply this excluded-area hours ratio by total overhead salaries and hours reported on Lines 26 through 43 of Worksheet S-3, Part II to compute overhead salaries and hours allocated to excluded areas. Then compute associated overhead wage-related costs (see overhead rate criterion). Finally subtract the computed excluded-area overhead salaries, wage-related costs, and hours from totals derived in Steps 2 and 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overhead Rate and exclusion of contract labor from overhead wage-related costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the overhead rate (from Worksheet S-3, Part II) as the ratio of overhead hours (Lines 26 through 43 minus the sum of Lines 28, 33, and 35) to revised hours excluding the sum of lines 28, 33, and 35. Formula: (Lines 26 through 43 − Lines 28, 33 and 35)/((((Line 1 + Lines 28, 33, 35) − (Lines 2, 3, 4.01, 5, 6, 7, 7.01, 8, and 26 through 43)) − (Lines 9 and 10)) + (Lines 26 through 43 − Lines 28, 33, and 35)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude overhead contract labor (Lines 28, 33, 35) from the denominator because hospitals typically do not provide fringe benefits to contract personnel; if a hospital does contribute wage-related costs for contracted personnel, instructions require combining those wage-related costs with wages on the respective contract labor lines. Use the overhead rate to multiply by wage-related costs reported on Part II, Lines 17, 22, 25.50, 25.51, and 25.52 to compute overhead wage-related costs, then apply excluded-area hours ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute overhead wage-related costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute overhead wage-related costs by multiplying the overhead hours ratio by wage-related costs reported on Part II, Lines 17, 22, 25.50, 25.51, and 25.52, then multiply the computed overhead wage-related costs by the excluded area hours ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After computing, subtract the computed overhead salaries, wage-related costs, and hours associated with excluded areas from the total salaries (plus wage-related costs) and hours derived in prior steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage adjustment to a common period using the Employment Cost Index (Step 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust each hospital’s total salaries plus wage-related costs to a common period by estimating the percentage change in the ECI for compensation for each 30-day increment (for FY 2027: from October 14, 2022, through April 15, 2024) for private industry hospital workers using BLS Office of Compensation and Working Conditions data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ECI because it reflects total compensation (salaries plus fringe benefits) and includes managers. Use actual quarterly ECI data and base adjustment factors on the midpoint of the hospital's cost reporting period. CMS is not proposing changes to use of the ECI for FY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment to labor market areas and aggregation (Step 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign each hospital to its appropriate urban or rural labor market area before any reclassifications under specified statutory sections. Within each labor market area, add the total adjusted salaries plus wage-related costs (from Step 5) for all hospitals in that area to determine the area total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment occurs prior to any reclassifications; aggregated area totals are used in subsequent average wage computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute area average hourly wage (Step 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the total adjusted salaries plus wage-related costs for a labor market area (Step 6) by the sum of the corresponding total hours (from Step 4) for all hospitals in the area to determine an average hourly wage for the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the area average as the numerator in the wage index calculation in Step 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute national average hourly wage (Step 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum the total adjusted salaries plus wage-related costs obtained in Step 5 for all hospitals in the Nation and divide by the national sum of total hours from Step 4 to arrive at a national average hourly wage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This national average (unadjusted for occupational mix) is used to normalize area wages to create wage indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute unadjusted hospital wage index (Step 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each urban or rural labor market area, calculate the hospital wage index value, unadjusted for occupational mix, by dividing the area average hourly wage (Step 7) by the national average hourly wage (Step 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields the basic unadjusted wage index used before occupational mix and other adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for urban CBSAs with no hospital wage data (Step 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each urban labor market area with no hospital wage data, calculate the CBSA wage index as: total urban salaries plus wage-related costs in the State (from Step 5) divided by total urban hours in the State (from Step 4), divided by the national average hourly wage (from Step 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considers a statewide urban average based on acceptable wage data more reasonable than imputing other values. For FY 2027 they applied this for one CBSA and footnoted Table 3. See Appendix B for rural-area policies. Round as described in rounding policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding policy for wage index calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: For 'raw data' (cost report Worksheets S-3 Parts II and III, and occupational mix survey data) use data 'as is' (no rounding). For any dollar amounts within wage index calculations round to 2 decimals. Round hour amounts to the nearest whole number. Round numbers not expressed as dollars or hours (ratios, percentages, inflation factors) to 5 decimals. Round the actual unadjusted and adjusted wage indexes to 4 decimals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy ensures consistency across calculations and was finalized in the FY 2020 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule; apply uniformly to both unadjusted and occupational mix–adjusted computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puerto Rico wage index policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No Puerto Rico–specific overall average hourly wage or wage index for FY 2027; Puerto Rico hospitals are subject to the national average hourly wage and the national wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Puerto Rico hospitals are now paid 100 percent of the national standardized amount (since Jan 1, 2016), CMS no longer calculates a Puerto Rico–specific wage index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupational mix data collection frequency and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect occupational mix data every 3 years for each short-term, acute care hospital participating in Medicare (statutory requirement). The CY 2022 survey used Form CMS-10079 (OMB Control Number 0938-0907) with hospitals required to submit completed 2022 surveys by July 1, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary unaudited survey data were posted on the CMS website July 12, 2023. The occupational mix measurement is required for constructing the occupational mix adjustment to the wage index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 2022 occupational mix survey for FY 2027 and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The FY 2027 occupational mix adjustment is based on the CY 2022 occupational mix survey. CMS proposes to calculate the occupational mix adjustment factor using the same methodology used since FY 2012 and to apply the occupational mix adjustment to 100 percent of the FY 2027 wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rounding conventions for occupational mix computations follow the rounding policy specified earlier. The FY 2022 survey data underpin the occupational mix–adjusted national average hourly wages used in the FY 2027 calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupational mix survey compliance and proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: All hospitals subject to IPPS payments must complete the occupational mix survey unless the hospital has no associated cost report wage data included in the wage index. For FY 2027 CMS used Worksheet S-3 wage data of 3,006 hospitals and occupational mix surveys of 2,922 hospitals (97% response). CMS applies proxy data for noncompliant hospitals, new hospitals, or hospitals submitting erroneous or aberrant data as done in FY 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proxy methodology follows precedent; CMS may revise or verify survey data as part of development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multicampus hospital allocation for occupational mix and wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Salaries and hours for multicampus hospitals are allotted among the different labor market areas where campuses are located; Table 2 includes separate wage data for campuses and CMS lists FTE percentages used to allot occupational mix data. Hospitals must identify and allocate wages and hours for remote locations in different CBSAs on Worksheet S-2, Part I, Lines 165 and 166 of form CMS-2552-10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote locations of hospitals with §412.103 rural reclassification status in a different CBSA are identified in Table 2 with a 'B' in the 3rd position of the CCN; hospitals should evaluate wage index outcomes for remote locations when changing reclassification status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of nurse-category average on occupational mix adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals with a nurse category average hourly wage greater than the national nurse category average (as calculated in Step 4) receive an occupational mix adjustment factor of less than 1.0; hospitals with a nurse category average less than the national nurse category average receive an occupational mix adjustment factor greater than 1.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism controls for hospital employment choices (mix of nursing staff) as reflecting management decisions rather than geographic wage differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement and timing for CY2025 occupational mix survey (for FY 2028)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new occupational mix measurement is required for FY 2028 based on a CY 2025 survey (Form CMS-10079). Hospitals are required to submit completed 2025 surveys to their MACs by June 30, 2026; preliminary unaudited CY 2025 data will be posted mid-July 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form has OMB approval and CMS/MACs may revise/verify survey elements during wage index development.

rubrics_metrics.name: §412.103 urban-to-rural reclassification substantive rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1886(d)(8)(E) and §412.103, a qualifying prospective payment hospital located in an urban area may apply for rural status for payment purposes, and if the hospital satisfies certain criteria the Secretary shall treat the hospital as being located in the rural area not later than 60 days after receipt of an application. Refer to §412.103 for general criteria and application requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §412.103 reclassifications apply to entire hospital (main campus and remote locations). A main campus cannot obtain SCH, RRC, MDH status, or §412.103 rural reclassification independently of remote locations, and vice versa, except as clarified in §412.103(a)(8). Reclassification remains in effect unless circumstances change (e.g., no longer in a rural census tract per FORHP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on terminated/tied-out hospitals and §412.103 reclassification for wage index
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS finalized a policy that §412.103 reclassifications are considered cancelled for purposes of calculating the area wage index for any hospital with a CCN listed as terminated or 'tied-out' as of the date the hospital ceased to operate with an active CCN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will obtain CCN termination status lists as of the §412.103(b)(6) 'lock-in' date (60 days after the proposed rule is displayed in the Federal Register) to determine inclusion in wage index development. This policy does not affect CAH, SCH, or REH qualification outside wage index calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: MGCRB reclassification application timing and procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1886(d)(10) the MGCRB considers geographic reclassification applications; hospitals must apply not later than 13 months prior to the start of the fiscal year for which reclassification is sought (usually by September 1). The MGCRB generally requires proximity to the labor market area and demonstration of characteristics similar to hospitals in that area. The MGCRB issues decisions not later than the end of February for reclassifications effective the following fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant regulations are at §§412.230–412.280; CMS publishes a 'Three Year MGCRB Reclassification Data Applications' file during each cycle. Use of three-year data improves consistency and reduces aberrant-year impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and termination rules for MGCRB applications (§412.273)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals that have applied to the MGCRB may withdraw applications any time before the MGCRB issues a decision. Hospitals may terminate an approved reclassification after MGCRB decision provided the request for termination is received within 45 days of the date of filing for public inspection of the proposed rule, or within 7 calendar days of receiving the Administrator's decision, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §412.273 and cited prior rules for current procedures and timelines; applications for FY 2028 are due to the MGCRB by September 1, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous §412.103 and MGCRB reclassification policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations permit hospitals to have simultaneous §412.103 urban-to-rural and MGCRB reclassifications. If both are active, the MGCRB reclassification controls for wage index calculation and payment purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits hospitals to obtain the broader rural benefits of §412.103 while pursuing MGCRB reclassification benefits. Prior to the regulatory amendment hospitals had to choose between the two.

rubrics_metrics.name: MGCRB proximity/mileage mapping requirement and inclusion of ferry routes (proposed revision to §412.230(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The MGCRB requires evidence of the shortest route over improved roads to the area and the distance as proximity data, traditionally measured by shortest route over improved roads maintained by government entities. CMS proposes to modify §412.230(c)(1) to include waterways traveled by ferry boats as equivalent to improved roads when mapping the shortest route, requiring map evidence from nationally recognized electronic mapping services showing the shortest route over improved roads or waterways traveled by ferry boats from the hospital front entrance to the county line of the requested area and the distance of that route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying the same measurement method for ferry miles as land miles should reduce appeals; mapping must be from recognized electronic mapping services (e.g., Google Maps, Bing Maps, MapQuest). CMS seeks comment on this proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year weighted average data requirement for MGCRB reclassification approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating reclassification requests, the MGCRB must use the average of the most recent hospital wage survey data and the data from each of the two immediately preceding surveys (three-year weighted average). CMS states its longstanding position that three-year weighted average data is required for approval by the MGCRB for all average hourly wage criteria under §412.230.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS publishes three-year data during application cycles; using three-year data improves consistency and reduces the impact of single-year aberrant data.

rubrics_metrics.name: MGCRB data publication and reclassification data file
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS publishes a 'Three Year MGCRB Reclassification Data Applications' file during each application cycle on the CMS website to provide the data used for application evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use that CMS-published data as the authoritative dataset when preparing reclassification submissions.
